from pagination import paginate


def test_literal_example_range_1_8_page_2_size_2():
    # Literal issue example: range(1, 8) -> [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7]
    result = paginate(range(1, 8), 2, 2)
    assert result == [3, 4]
    assert isinstance(result, list)


def test_first_page_is_one_based():
    assert paginate(range(1, 8), 1, 2) == [1, 2]


def test_last_full_page():
    assert paginate(range(1, 8), 3, 2) == [5, 6]


def test_partial_last_page():
    assert paginate(range(1, 8), 4, 2) == [7]


def test_beyond_last_page_returns_empty_list():
    result = paginate(range(1, 8), 5, 2)
    assert result == []
    assert isinstance(result, list)


def test_empty_input_returns_empty_list():
    result = paginate([], 1, 2)
    assert result == []
    assert isinstance(result, list)


def test_invalid_page_returns_empty_list():
    assert paginate([1, 2], 0, 2) == []
    assert paginate([1, 2], -1, 2) == []


def test_invalid_page_size_returns_empty_list():
    assert paginate([1, 2], 1, 0) == []
    assert paginate([1, 2], 1, -3) == []


def test_input_list_is_not_mutated():
    items = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7]
    snapshot = list(items)
    paginate(items, 2, 2)
    assert items == snapshot


def test_page_size_larger_than_input():
    assert paginate(range(1, 8), 1, 100) == [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7]
    assert paginate(range(1, 8), 2, 100) == []

patches.rationale: The bug: paginate computes start = page * page_size, which is zero-based indexing applied to one-based page numbers, so page 1 returns items[page_size:2*page_size] and page 2 returns items[2*page_size:3*page_size]. For range(1,8) (i.e. [1,2,3,4,5,6,7]), page 2 size 2 currently returns [5,6] instead of [3,4]. Fix: start = (page - 1) * page_size. Empty/invalid inputs (page < 1 or page_size < 1) still return [], and slicing beyond the last page naturally returns []. Existing tests remain valid: paginate([],1,2) == [] and paginate([1,2],0,2) == []. Add a new regression test file tests/test_pagination_regression.py covering the literal example range(1,8) page 2 size 2 -> [3,4], plus boundary behavior (first page, last page, beyond last page, invalid inputs, empty input) and preservation of input list (no mutation).
